title: Community or custom editor data
description: Content stored by non-core property editors whose data format belongs to a package or to custom code.

impact.summary: Third-party editor data is carried over as stored in 7, and custom editor configuration may need custom migrators.

sources.evidence: Umbraco has no way of knowing how custom property editors have intended to structure their configuration data
The migration will transform the data stored in third party editors as well

impact.summary: Property editors split into a server schema and a client UI; data types migrate on upgrade and AngularJS editor UIs are rebuilt.

sources.evidence: Umbraco 14 introduces a split between server-side and client-side Property Editor aliases
Umbraco automatically migrates all Data Types to include an EditorUiAlias value
AngularJS code does not run in the new backoffice, so you rebuild each extension

handling.option: Use the package release for the target (checked through package metadata)
handling.when: A release exists for the target

sources.evidence: This article will cover the process of installing as well as uninstalling packages from your Umbraco CMS website

handling.option: Convert the data to a core editor with a migration tested on the local copy
handling.when: No release exists, or a core editor covers the need

handling.option: Keep a custom editor: a new UI plus a server-side schema for the stored data

sources.evidence: Umbraco 14 introduces a split between server-side and client-side Property Editor aliases
Since the migration moves the alias to EditorUiAlias

checks.text: Every data type that used the editor shows and saves its data in the backoffice of the local site
